contributions.statement: Budget the tools visible in one agent context by model class: about 10 for Haiku-class models and about 20 for Sonnet-class. Above that, expose a per-task subset rather than the merged catalog, and re-measure on your own tools before treating the number as a limit.
contributions.evidence: §VI-C, Fig. 2: production telemetry, N=200 turns per bucket, human-confirmed ground truth; Haiku 91%@10 vs 87%@15 (±4 pp, overlapping), Sonnet ≥90% to 20 and below at 30; model and tool count confounded by tenant; raw logs unreleased.
relative_to: P03 deferred tool loading / small tool catalog
Gan & Sun (>90% up to ~30 tools, pre-2026)

contributions.statement: A static-merge MCP aggregator that surfaces the union of upstream tools raises the visible tool count past the selection budget; if aggregation is needed, scope tools per request.
contributions.evidence: §IV-D, §VI-C: argued from the tool-count curve; no aggregator was evaluated.
relative_to: P03 deferred tool loading / small tool catalog

contributions.statement: In-host MCP transport overhead is under 0.5 ms (stdio 0.01 ms, loopback HTTP 0.39 ms p50); latency decisions hinge on co-location and extra network hops, not transport encoding.
contributions.evidence: Table III measured rows (N=100 echo calls); hop costs are modeled.
relative_to: network RTT dominates local IPC overhead (standard systems knowledge)

contributions.statement: Avoid God tools (do_anything(action, params)) and name-only tool descriptions; give each operation its own named tool with a description of what, when and returns.
relative_to: Anthropic and OpenAI tool-use documentation guidance

reason: The tool budget is the one actionable number, and it is new at the small-catalog scale. But it comes from confounded, unauditable telemetry with overlapping CIs at the threshold, so it stands as a hypothesis to re-measure, not a gate. The patterns and anti-patterns are renamed GoF/EIP structures or vendor guidance.
